summary: @servicetitan/help-center preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares a preinstall script `node setup.mjs` that runs automatically on `npm install`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime binary (bun-v1.3.13) from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts it, chmods it executable, and then invokes it via execFileSync against the sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a ~727KB heavily obfuscated `@bun @bun-cjs` blob using rotated string-array obfuscation and mangled identifiers, with no corresponding TypeScript source in src/ and no relationship to the package's advertised React help-center functionality. The rest of the tarball ships plausible-looking React component source as cover. The use of an alternate JavaScript runtime (Bun) rather than Node is characteristic of droppers designed to evade Node-based scanning, and executing a large opaque obfuscated payload at install time under a freshly downloaded runtime is the alternate-runtime-dropper attack pattern.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
